pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all 3 seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected. Migrations are re-applied before each test.
'AC-2' asserts the list is [First item, ★ Second item, Third item]. It would fail if the ★ were missing or on the wrong item.
'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects [★ First item, ★ Third item] with status 200. That checks the filter and the id order.
'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all give all items in id order.
'AC-5' checks the exact 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on the starred view.
'AC-6' sends Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. Each must give 400 with no <li>. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is rejected.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic worker passes route strings straight to fetch, so the query is preserved, and the config check now accepts it.

findings.what: The README mentions ?show=starred but not that other show values answer 400, nor the ★ marker.
findings.fix: Add one clause saying show accepts all or starred and anything else is a 400.

lenses.note: The spec has an owner go dated 2026-10-12. The change matches its decisions: order is unchanged and the view is a query parameter. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-check regex relaxation, which AC-7 needs and the PR discloses.
All 7 AC items are named by tests. All 4 state-table rows have a test. The spec was added in the same change, with no later edit to the acceptance items.

Assertions check behaviour: list contents, status codes, messages and links. The traffic fake now records the query; that is disclosed and no assertion is weakened. tests/traffic-config.test.sh adds reject cases for a fragment and a space, and a pass case for a query string. I did not run the tests here; CI covers that.
The README was updated. One low gap, noted in the finding.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn. The SQL is built only from fixed view fragments, with no user input. Both empty states are handled.
The show value is never interpolated into SQL or HTML. Titles are still escaped. No instructions were planted in the content under review.
The page is a minimal server-rendered list with no stylesheet or UI framework files. QA and design review do not apply.
The diff touches no UI components or styles, and there is no browser in the session.

The title is under 72 characters. The behaviour, test and traffic-check claims match the diff. 'Changed after the go: nothing' holds, since the spec was added in the same change with the go already recorded.
